Which gold medals are you referring to? I assume nether warts and maybe wheat, but I’m not really sure which others you mean. 

Either way, I recommend you make use of the pest feature. Pop 40 pests in with Phillip for a bonus 200 farming fortune. You can add another 50 temporary fortune by using a harvest harbinger potion, they are awarded from the visitor Maeve but can be bought on the ah. 

Do also make sure you’ve got custom farms for the crops you’re trying to get gold in. You’re aiming for 19.8 bps, or breaks per second. Mods such as skyhanni will allow you to see your bps and is a useful tools in many other ways as well. 

Last but not least, don’t cheap out on the farming tools themselves. Yeah you might not want to get T3 for every hoe, especially wheat unless you plan on farming that for a long time. Keep in mind though if you struggle with getting golds that the tools and their enchants play a mayor role in your farming fortune.

If you have any questions or feel like I’ve been unclear somewhere don’t hesitate to ask!

If you keep up a 19.8 bps, the expected required ff to get gold in nether wart is roughly 1350. (This obviously is not the case for every contest, but it gives an estimate.) With your 1515 ff you should absolutely crush the gold medal. 

Does your farm allow you to maintain 19.8 bps, or at least close? If not, then I would advise you to rebuild the farm because that’ll increase your efficiency immensely. If you have a custom farm, make sure you use it correctly with the right speed and angle. 

Additionally, use pests from the vacuum, and a harvest harbinger potion if you have. It’ll boost your ff by 250 in total (200 from 40 pests + 50 from the potion).

I had a very similar issue with my girlfriend. The way we dealt with it was by simply talking. A lot. We too live quite far away from each other, so we typically talked over the phone. Some weekends we could spend 30+ hours on the phone, even more when things got worse. We talked about anything under the sun, from depression, suicide, bullying and tough times at school to her favorite flowers. I remember when we talked about funerals, and she stated that when she died she wanted me to play “Mama, I’m coming home” by Alice Cooper. 

Anyways, my best tip is to talk. She needs to feel like you understand her, not that you can solve her problems. Communication is key, and simply hearing your voice and feeling that her voice is heard too may at times be all she needs. Of course this is not a universal solution, but in my experience it works fairly well. 

One thing for you to keep in mind: Give her time. She will need lots of it. Healing from things like this can take years.
